# sphinx-searchlite

Client-side documentation search for any Sphinx theme. It needs no search
service, no runtime dependency, and no build step beyond Sphinx itself.

[![Build Status](https://github.com/python-project-templates/sphinx-searchlite/actions/workflows/build.yaml/badge.svg?branch=main&event=push)](https://github.com/python-project-templates/sphinx-searchlite/actions/workflows/build.yaml)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/python-project-templates/sphinx-searchlite/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/python-project-templates/sphinx-searchlite)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/python-project-templates/sphinx-searchlite)](https://github.com/python-project-templates/sphinx-searchlite)
[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/sphinx-searchlite.svg)](https://pypi.python.org/pypi/sphinx-searchlite)

## Quick start

Install the package:

```bash
pip install sphinx-searchlite
```

Add it to `conf.py`:

```python
extensions = ["sphinx_searchlite"]
```

Build your docs and open any page. Press `/` or `⌘K` (`Ctrl+K` on Linux and
Windows) to open the search dialog. If your theme has its own search box,
clicking it opens the same dialog.

## Documentation

- [How-to guides](docs/src/how-to.html.md): keep the theme’s search box, write your
  own UI, add triggers, and restyle the dialog.
- [Reference](docs/src/reference.html.md): configuration options, the JavaScript
  API, the index format, and CSS custom properties.
- [Explanation](docs/src/explanation.html.md): why searchlite exists, how ranking
  works, and how the dialog picks its colors.

This library was generated using [copier](https://copier.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) from the [Base Python Project Template repository](https://github.com/python-project-templates/base).

<!-- docs/src/how-to.html.md -->

# How-to guides

## Keep the theme’s own search box

By default searchlite takes over the theme’s search box so that it opens the
dialog. To leave the box wired to Sphinx’s `search.html`, set:

```python
searchlite_adopt_theme_search = False
```

The dialog still opens with `/` and `⌘K`, and from any element with
`data-searchlite-open`.

## Add a button that opens the dialog

Add the `data-searchlite-open` attribute to any element in your templates:

```html
<button type="button" data-searchlite-open>Search</button>
```

## Use your own search UI

Turn off the bundled dialog so only the engine is shipped:

```python
searchlite_ui = False
```

Then query the engine from your own script:

```js
const engine = SearchLite.create({ url: SearchLite.indexUrl });

await engine.load();
const { items, terms } = engine.search("query");

for (const item of items) {
  const snippet = SearchLite.highlight(SearchLite.excerpt(item, terms), terms);
  // render item.u, item.t, item.s, and snippet
}
```

See the [JavaScript API](reference.html.md#javascript-api) for what each call
returns.

## Restyle the dialog

Set `--searchlite-*` custom properties on `#searchlite-dialog`:

```css
#searchlite-dialog {
  --searchlite-background: #111;
  --searchlite-foreground: #eee;
  --searchlite-radius: 0.25rem;
}
```

Target the dialog element rather than `:root`. The dialog copies the page’s
colors onto itself at runtime, and those inline values override anything
inherited from `:root`. Setting the background and foreground is usually
enough, because the muted, border, and accent colors are mixed from the
foreground.

<!-- docs/src/reference.html.md -->

# Reference

## Configuration

Set these in `conf.py`.

| Option                          | Default                 | Description                                                                                 |
|---------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `searchlite_index_filename`     | `searchlite-index.json` | Name of the index file written to `_static/`.                                               |
| `searchlite_max_text`           | `1200`                  | Maximum characters of body text kept per record.                                            |
| `searchlite_ui`                 | `True`                  | Ship the bundled dialog and its CSS. When `False`, only the engine is shipped.              |
| `searchlite_adopt_theme_search` | `True`                  | Make the theme’s search box open the dialog. Has no effect when `searchlite_ui` is `False`. |

## Index format

The index is a JSON array of records. Each page produces one record for the
page, one for each section that has an anchor, and one for each object
description that has an anchor, such as an autodoc class, method or attribute.

| Key   | Description                                                                                                             |
|-------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `u`   | URL relative to the documentation root, with `#anchor` for sections and objects.                                        |
| `t`   | Title of the page.                                                                                                      |
| `s`   | Section heading, or the object’s full name. Absent on page records.                                                     |
| `x`   | Text, truncated to `searchlite_max_text`. Sections exclude nested sections and objects; objects exclude nested objects. |

`engine.load()` rewrites `u` to an absolute URL.

## JavaScript API

The engine defines a global `SearchLite` object.

### `SearchLite.create({ url })`

Returns an engine for the index at `url`. Nothing is fetched until `load()` is
called.

### `engine.load()`

Fetches and indexes the records. Returns a promise. Repeated calls return the
same promise. A failed fetch produces an empty index.

### `engine.ready()`

Returns `true` once the index is built.

### `engine.search(query)`

Returns `{ items, terms }`. `items` is an array of up to 20 records, best match
first. `terms` lists the index terms that matched, including prefix expansions.
Returns empty arrays if the index is not loaded or the query has no words.

### `SearchLite.indexUrl`

Absolute URL of the index for the current page, or `null` if it cannot be
resolved.

### `SearchLite.tokenize(text)`

Returns the lowercase words in `text`, split on anything other than `a-z`,
`0-9`, and `_`.

### `SearchLite.excerpt(record, terms, length = 120)`

Returns about `length` characters of `record.x`, starting just before the first
matching term. Prefixed with `…` when it does not start at the beginning.

### `SearchLite.highlight(text, terms)`

Returns a `DocumentFragment` of `text` with each match wrapped in `<mark>`.

## Dialog

| Key                 | Action                     |
|---------------------|----------------------------|
| `/`, `⌘K`, `Ctrl+K` | Open the dialog.           |
| `↑`, `↓`            | Move between results.      |
| `Enter`             | Go to the selected result. |
| `Escape`            | Close the dialog.          |

Any element with the `data-searchlite-open` attribute opens the dialog when
clicked.

## CSS custom properties

| Property                  | Default                           | Set on                   |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------|
| `--searchlite-background` | `#fff`, or the page background    | `:root`, then the dialog |
| `--searchlite-foreground` | `#18181b`, or the page text color | `:root`, then the dialog |
| `--searchlite-radius`     | `0.75rem`                         | `:root`                  |
| `--searchlite-muted`      | foreground at 60%                 | `#searchlite-dialog`     |
| `--searchlite-border`     | foreground at 20%                 | `#searchlite-dialog`     |
| `--searchlite-accent`     | foreground at 10%                 | `#searchlite-dialog`     |

<!-- docs/src/explanation.html.md -->

# Explanation

## Why not Sphinx’s own search?

Sphinx ships `searchindex.js`, but it is tied to `searchtools.js` and the
dedicated `search.html` page, and there is no supported way to query it from
your own UI. searchlite writes plain JSON records instead, so a theme can score
and render results however it likes.

## How ranking works

Results are scored with BM25 over the record text, with extra weight for two
fields:

- the record’s own heading, weighted heavily
- the title of the page it belongs to, weighted lightly

These are kept separate because every section of a page shares that page’s
title. If both were weighted heavily, searching for a page title would rank
its subsections alongside the page itself, often above it.

The last word of the query is matched as a prefix as well as exactly, since
you are probably still typing it. That way `install` also finds
`installation`. Results must match every query word that appears in the index,
so adding words narrows the results. Words that appear nowhere in the index are
ignored.

## Why the dialog takes over the theme’s search box

Most themes render a search box that submits to `search.html`. Left alone, a
page would have two different searches, and the dialog would have no visible
way to open it. searchlite makes that box read-only and opens the dialog when
it is clicked, activated with `Enter` or `Space`, or its form is submitted.
It does not open on focus, because closing the dialog returns focus to the box,
which would open it again.

## How the dialog picks its colors

The dialog reads the page’s background and text colors and copies them onto
itself. It watches for changes, so it follows the theme’s light and dark
toggle. Most themes switch modes with a class or attribute, which
`prefers-color-scheme` does not detect.

<!-- autoapi/sphinx_searchlite/index.html.md -->

# sphinx_searchlite

Client-side documentation search for any Sphinx theme.

Emits a small JSON index next to the build and ships a dependency-free BM25
engine to score it in the browser. Themes can either use the bundled dialog or
drive `window.SearchLite` themselves.

Return one record for the page plus one per addressable section and object description.

Keys are short because the index ships to the browser: `u` url, `t` page
title, `s` section heading, `x` text.

# sphinx_searchlite._index

Build the client-side search index.

Sphinx’s own `searchindex.js` is coupled to `searchtools.js` and its
dedicated `search.html` page. This emits plain records any front end can
score itself, keyed so that section anchors survive incremental builds.

## Functions

| [`collect_records`](#sphinx_searchlite._index.collect_records)(→ list[dict[str, str]])   | Return one record for the page plus one per addressable section and object description.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`setup_index`](#sphinx_searchlite._index.setup_index)(→ None)                           |                                                                                           |
